A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpecReason research. Their text and figures are readable, and all supplied pages were compared, including v2 Appendix A. V1 has no appendix; its R1-70B study is retained in v2's appendix.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.5 report original accuracy and latency measurements, threshold experiments, R1-70B evaluation, and comparisons with process reward model scores.

after.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4 and Appendix A report original benchmark results across multiple model pairings, token-budget and output-length analyses, and inference-control experiments.

M1.justification: V2 Section 4.1 introduces an optional control that forces the base model to generate the first n reasoning steps before speculation. The core proposal, utility scoring, threshold acceptance, fallback regeneration, and hierarchical speculative decoding procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AIME 2024, MATH500, and GPQA Diamond. The added model pairings, token budgets, and control experiments remain within these mathematical and scientific reasoning tasks. Adding GPQA to the threshold analysis does not introduce a previously unevaluated task.

E2.justification: Matched main comparisons retain vanilla base-model inference, vanilla small-model inference, SpecDecode, and SpecReason+Decode. V2 applies these schemes to additional model configurations. Math-Shepherd remains the scoring comparator; newly cited token-cache methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: The main evaluation expands from QwQ-32B/R1-1.5B to four pairings by adding Skywork-OR1-Preview-32B and ZR1-1.5B. V2 also measures thinking-token counts, varies token budgets, tests n=0,10,20,30,40 initial base-model steps, and extends the threshold sweep from 3,5,7 to include 9. The main pass@1 metric, 8192-token budget, and hardware setup remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds output-length comparisons across model pairings (Figures 4a and 9), AIME token-budget sensitivity (Figure 4b), and the initial-base-model-step experiment (Figure 6). Its threshold analysis adds GPQA and threshold 9. The existing R1-70B and process reward model analyses are retained, with the former moved to Appendix A.1.

E5.justification: Both versions calculate accuracy from 16 responses per query at temperature 0.6. Neither reports seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates and averages.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for three main model pairings and the new supplementary analyses. Existing reported values also change: QwQ-32B/R1-1.5B accuracy gains change from 1.0%, 3.1%, and 9.9% to a reported range of 1.3%–3.6%. AIME accuracies at thresholds 3 and 7 change from 22.9% and 40.5% to 22.3% and 39.3%. These are revised reported estimates, not evidence of a uniform performance improvement.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs, or acceleration guarantees. The mathematical examples remain illustrative reasoning equations. The new controls and empirical analyses do not add formal mathematical results.

C1.justification: The central claims about semantic speculation and compatibility with speculative decoding remain. The abstract and conclusion revise the claimed speedup from 1.5–2.5× to 1.4–3.0×, accuracy improvement from 1.0–9.9% to 0.4–9.0%, and additional latency reduction over speculative decoding from 19.4–44.2% to 8.8–58.0%.

C2.justification: V1 attributes accuracy gains primarily to explicit scoring augmenting self-reflection. V2 makes reduced token consumption under a fixed budget the primary explanation, while retaining scoring as another contributor. Figure 4b shows the reported AIME advantage shrinking from 16.2% at 4096 tokens to 4.7% at 8192. V2 also discusses Skywork's weaker instruction following and consequent need for stricter acceptance thresholds.

D1.justification: V2 documents the added model identities and configuration values for new experiments, including the initial-step sweep n=0,10,20,30,40. Existing vLLM 0.8.2, GPU and tensor-parallel settings, cache handling, sequential execution, and repository access information remain unchanged. The added details do not establish a change to the underlying inference engine.

R1.justification: V2 adds references and discussion covering SuffixDecoding, token recycling, Lookahead, and additional reasoning models. It also contrasts SpecReason with distillation, token-budget restriction, and disabling reasoning. Existing Sky-T1-Flash and Dynasor-CoT references are retained in Background, although their earlier explicit relationship statements are shortened.

P1.justification: The Introduction and Motivation undergo extensive paragraph rewriting, and Section 4.1 reorganizes the method explanation around inference controls. Related Work is incorporated into Background, an evaluation overview is added, and the R1-70B section moves to Appendix A.1. These substantially revise the existing narrative and organization.

P2.justification: Figure 3 expands from three panels to twelve organized by model pairing. V2 adds token-length, token-budget, and initial-step-control figures, expands the threshold plot to include GPQA, and supplies the full token-length comparison in Appendix Figure 9. The R1-70B figure is relocated, and the process reward model plot is resized beside the new control plot.

improvement.justification: V1's accuracy-gain explanation relied mainly on an untested attribution to scoring and results from one principal model pairing. V2's token-length and budget experiments provide substantive evidence about when those gains arise, while the expanded model matrix reduces dependence on that pairing. Together these substantially strengthen the support and interpretation of the central claims, with the earlier R1-70B and critic checks retained. Statistical uncertainty remains unreported.
